newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch suspend wheat futures contract - trade.
newsitem.headline: Dutch suspend wheat futures contract - trade.

text.p: The Amsterdam Agricultural Futures Exchange (ATA) has suspended its wheat futures contracts indefinitely, trade sources said on Friday.
"This morning a note was handed around saying the (wheat) contracts would stop trading for a time," a trade source said.
No-one at the exchange was immediately available for comment.
The fledgling milling wheat contracts, launched in June, have consistently failed to attract interest. On some days, recently, turnover has been nil.
"There was no market for it, using Chicago was more liquid, more easy to use," the trade source said. "Market conditions have not been favourable."

In the early stages, the ATA blamed the lacklustre performance of the contracts on the timing of the launch, comning in between harvests. It said earlier this month it was reviewing the contracts' specifications, focusing on quality and the size of lots traded -- 125 tonnes.
